{
  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study proposes a Bayesian approach to toxicological testing, focusing on predicting toxicity (cardiac arrhythmia torsade de pointes) based on test results and their predictive power. It discusses combining tests to achieve desired predictive power, which implies a quantitative measure of agreement between test outcomes and actual toxicity, aligning with the review's criteria for including studies that report agreement statistics.",
  "arm": "toxicology",
  "arm_evidence": "Testing for toxicities is an important activity in drug development.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "cardiovascular",
    "cross-cutting"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "We use as examples tests available for the prediction of a substance's liability to cause the cardiac arrhythmia torsade de pointes.",
  "model_type": "across-multiple-models",
  "model_evidence": "The proposed approach is easily implemented deterministically since values of the discriminatory power of the tests are readily and publicly available.",
  "species": [
    "not-species-specific"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "The text discusses general testing schemes and predictive power without specifying any particular animal species used in the tests being analyzed.",
  "endpoint_class": "mixed",
  "endpoint_evidence": "A test's discriminatory power is characterized by its sensitivity and specificity... The investigator is, however, more interested in a test's predictive power..."
}
